card.name: Time unit before 'intervals' or frequency
card.fires_on: The time word or linking word just before a monitoring or dosing schedule is completed, such as week or year before 'intervals', 'a' before 'year', or 'of' after 'frequency'. It appears in label instructions about how often to measure or adjust.

modes.label: Interval unit
modes.description: The time unit in a phrase like 'two-week intervals' or '2 to 3 year intervals'.
modes.example: Titrate the sevelamer carbonate dose by 0.8 g three times per day with meals at two<<-week>> intervals as necessary

modes.label: Frequency phrase
modes.description: A word inside a phrase about how often something is done, such as 'once a year' or 'frequency of monitoring'.
modes.example: Adults 60 or older should have an eye exam at least once<< a>> year to determine

modes.label: Weekly monitoring
modes.description: The word 'weekly' when monitoring is stepped up.
modes.example: Increase to<< weekly>> monitoring of liver function as recommended.

card.writes: It lowers the odds of words like regularly, periodically and regular, since the schedule is being spelled out.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label gives how often to check or repeat something, like every two weeks or once a year.
